newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer undaunted in quest for Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: Placer undaunted in quest for Bre-X.

text.p: Gold miner Placer Dome Inc said Tuesday it remains confident its US$5 billion proposal to merge with Bre-X Minerals Ltd will succeed despite efforts by rival Barrick Gold Corp to close a joint venture deal with Bre-X on its rich Busang gold field in Indonesia.
Placer spokesman Hugh Leggatt said comments by Barrick indicated the Toronto gold company believes it remains the Indonesian government's favored partner for Bre-X.
"We don't see it like that. We have a creative and compelling proposal on the table and we expect it will succeed," Leggatt said. "We are still very much in it."

He said Placer was "quietly working" on the ground on Indonesia to press its case. Asked if the Indonesian government had responded to Placer's merger idea, he said, "We have had nothing definitive we can disclose...publicly."
Previously Placer had said it had had no reply or acknowledgement from the government.
A hoped-for meeting with Bre-X to discuss the merger proposal has not yet been scheduled, Leggatt said.
Bre-X, which controls the rich Busang discovery, was directed by the Indonesian government to negotiate a deal with Barrck last year.
But the process has taken longer than investors expected and Placer last week sought to convince Indonesia to allow competing offers by annoucing its own proposal.
The Indonesian government on Monday sent a letter to Bre-X and Barrick giving them one month to finalize their deal and conclude agreements with local partners.

Barrick said Tuesday it was confident it could meet the deadline, that Placer's proposal could not affect progress on the Barrick deal and that the Indonesian government had reaffirmed its support for Barrick's participation.
